title: The loop stops rebuilding the app the user is playtesting
goal: While the user was trying the Measure tool, a runner rebuilt and killed the dev app underneath them, which ended their session and made macOS demand the Screen Recording permission again, because a screen-capture app that changes on disk has to be re-authorized. Verification by the loop must never disturb the app a person is using.
notes: Playtest 2026-08-23. Evidence: queue/loop.log shows runners calling Scripts/build-app.sh followed by pkill -f "Photonz Dev" three times in one task, and the dist binary timestamp moved to 16:37 while the user had the app open. Signing itself is healthy: one Photonz Dev cert, and the designated requirement pins identifier plus that cert leaf, so the grant would survive a rebuild if macOS did not separately re-verify screen-capture clients whose binary changed. The stopgap is the lock file plus a hard rule in the runner contract. The real fix is a separate probe bundle id (for example com.dzearing.photonz.probe) built to its own path, granted once, so loop verification and user playtesting never share an app. Scripts/build-app.sh already takes a dev variant path, so add a probe variant rather than a new script.
acceptance: A runner that needs a running app builds to its own bundle, with its own bundle id and its own output path, never dist/Photonz Dev.app
The users dev app keeps a stable code identity so its Screen Recording grant survives, and is only rebuilt when the user asks
queue/playtest.lock is honoured: while it exists no runner touches the users app at all
Running the loop through a task that needs the app, while the lock exists, leaves the users app untouched, verified by comparing its binary timestamp before and after
